entries.text: Thank you for calling VeloFit. Your call is important to us. Please hold while we connect you to the next available agent.
Thank you for holding. My name is David. How can I help you today?
I need to return something.
I can certainly help with that. Can I get your name and order number, please?
Sarah Miller. Order is VF-8675309.
Thank you, Sarah. One moment... Okay, I see your order for the VeloFit Pro-Lite cycling shoes. Is that what you're calling about?
Obviously.
Understood. To make sure I'm helping in the right way, could you tell me what specifically is the issue with the shoes? Is it a technical fault or more of a sizing or preference issue?
They're awful. I took them on one ride and they gave me terrible blisters.
I'm very sorry to hear that. Getting blisters is definitely not the experience we want for our customers. Did you have a chance to adjust the insoles or the position of the cleats?
Yes. I adjusted the cleats. It didn't help. The cycling shoes just don't fit. I want a refund.
Of course. I see here that the shoes were delivered five days ago, which is unfortunately outside our 10-day return policy for apparel and shoes. I can cannot offer a refund for you right away.
Fine. How does it work?

I'm sending a prepaid return label to the email address we have on file for you now. Just print that out, place the shoes back in their original box, attach the label, and you can drop it off at any UPS store.
And my money?

Once our warehouse receives and inspects the return, which usually takes 3-5 business days, we'll issue the refund to your original payment method. It can then take an additional 2-3 business days for your bank to post the funds to your account.
Whatever. Just make sure the label gets sent.
The email has just been sent. You should see it in your inbox shortly. Was there anything else I could assist you with today, Sarah?
No.
Alright. Thank you for calling VeloFit, and I hope we can find you a better-fitting pair of shoes in the future. Have a good rest of your day.
